chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

I was in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). Abbad al-Basri entered upon him, accompanied by some of his companions. He said to him, 'Narrate to me: when two men are taken in one quilt.' He (peace be upon him) said to him, 'Ali (peace be upon him), when he took two men in one quilt, would strike them with the Hadd (penalty).' Abbad said, 'You said to me: other than one lash.' So he repeated the mention of the hadith to him until he repeated it to him several times. Then he said, 'Other than one lash.' So the people present wrote down that hadith.

key_terms.الْحَدَّ: the fixed penalty prescribed by Sharia

ai.seo_question: What is the specific Hadd punishment for two men in one quilt according to Imam Ali (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the jurisprudential nuance in applying the *Hadd* punishment for illicit sexual relations (*Zina*), specifically addressing the scenario of two men sharing a single quilt (*Lihaaf*). It highlights the scholarly emphasis on precise transmission, as Imam al-Sadiq (AS) corrected the initial report of the full penalty to clarify it was 'other than one lash,' a distinction that sparked debate among companions like Abbad al-Basri regarding the exact nature of the deduction. This incident underscores the importance of verifying legal rulings through repeated confirmation to ensure accuracy in transmitting the Imam's precise legal stance.
